newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish car production rises by 14 pct in June.
newsitem.headline: Turkish car production rises by 14 pct in June.

text.p: Turkish passenger car production rose by 14 percent in June to 22,697 units, compared to June 1996, a statement by the Automotive Industry Association (OSD) said on Tuesday.

Car production over the first six months of 1997 rose by only one percent to 111,247 units from the same period of 1996, while overall motor vehicle output increased by nine percent to 180,478 units, the OSD said.

While overall car sales rose by 42 percent in the first six months of 1997 from first half 1996, sales of imported cars soared 137 percent, compared to an 18 percent sales increase in locally produced cars.
Thus, the market share of imported cars in the first half rose to a six-year high of 33 percent, the OSD said.

The biggest production increase was in the midibus category in January-June 1997 by 90 percent, followed by 57 percent in trucks, 47 percent in vans, 27 percent in buses and 25 percent in minibuses, compared to first half 1996, the OSD said.
Meanwhile, production of farm tractors declined by two percent to 25,658 in the first six months of this year.

The OSD said sales of light commercial vehicle imports also soared by 129 percent to 22,264 in the first half of 1997 while sales of locally produced vehicles rose by 55 percent to 17,437, compared to the the first six months of 1996.
Therefore, the market share of imported light commercial vehicles also rose to a six-year high of 56 percent in first half 1997.
The OSD said Turkey's total motor vehicle and parts exports fell by eight percent to $626.7 million in the first six months from $680.3 million in January-June 1996.
Vehicle exports were led by buses, down nine percent to $96.7 million and car exports, down 57 percent to $68.5 million.
Automotive part exports totalled $429.4 million, up nine percent from first half 1996. This included $120 million of tyre exports, down three percent.
